claims.reason: S1 directly defines checkpointing as transferring WAL transactions into the database.
S1 describes the commit record and its consequence: committing without writing the original database.
S1 specifies the 1000-page default and its compile-time configurability.
S1 supplies both the reader end-mark boundary and the overwrite hazard that requires stopping.
S1 explicitly describes saving checkpoint progress in the wal-index and resuming it. This does not state the rubric's shared-memory lookup and host restriction.
S1 specifies execution on the threshold-crossing commit's thread. The claim omits the slower-commit consequence required for full commit-latency coverage.
S1 explicitly distinguishes normal WAL reuse from truncation.
S1 states this ordered synchronization protocol. The claim does not explain its corruption-prevention consequence.
S1 states PASSIVE's default status and noninterference behavior. It does not cover both busy-handler avoidance and possible incompletion.
S1 explicitly identifies concurrent readers or writers as a condition that can leave PASSIVE unfinished. Busy-handler behavior is omitted.
S1 describes the final checkpoint and associated file cleanup when the last connection closes.
S2 specifies FULL's writer and reader waiting conditions and subsequent checkpoint and sync. The claim omits continued admission of new readers.
S2 states the precise asymmetry between new writers and readers while FULL is pending. It omits FULL's snapshot waiting condition.
S2 links waiting for database-only readers to the next writer restarting the log.
S2 defines TRUNCATE as RESTART plus zero-byte truncation before successful return.
S2 explicitly gives the contention condition, SQLITE_BUSY result, and absence of busy-handler invocation.
S2 explicitly excludes busy-handler invocation in PASSIVE. The claim omits possible checkpoint incompletion.
S2 describes configured busy-handler invocation and writer-lock retries when these modes cannot obtain the lock immediately.
S2 states that busy-handler refusal during writer-lock or reader waits causes PASSIVE-style progress and SQLITE_BUSY.
S2 defines NOOP as zero-frame checkpointing for retrieving the checkpoint status outputs.
S3 specifies the post-commit trigger at N or more frames. The claim does not state connection-local configuration.
S3 explicitly says non-positive N disables automatic checkpoints.
S3 describes reciprocal replacement between automatic checkpoint configuration and a WAL hook.
S1 explicitly identifies disabling automatic checkpointing as removing protection against excessive WAL growth.
S1 states the continuous overlapping-reader condition and both consequences: incomplete checkpoints and unbounded WAL growth.
S1 identifies reader-free intervals with checkpoint attempts as the mitigation for reader starvation.
S1 explicitly states that an ongoing write transaction prevents checkpoint completion and WAL reset.
S1 specifies the version boundary and expected proportional WAL size for a single transaction.
S1 identifies exceeding the page cache in older versions as the condition permitting repeated WAL writes of the same page.
S1 explicitly limits this sync behavior to synchronous=NORMAL. The claim omits the power-loss durability consequence.
The claim omits synchronous=NORMAL. S1 makes the no-main-thread-sync consequence conditional on NORMAL; FULL still syncs the WAL at commit.
The stated separate-checkpoint configuration does not specify synchronous=NORMAL. S1 attributes the durability tradeoff to that setting, not merely to moving checkpoints to another thread or process.
S1 describes the residual seeking cost despite ascending page-order writes.
S1 makes this comparison, but the claim supplies neither its I/O mechanism nor a specific limiting condition.
S1 connects frequent checkpoints and a small WAL to better read performance. The claim does not explain increased reader lookup cost or the opposing write cost.
S1 states the amortization mechanism. The claim gives the write benefit without stating the opposing read-performance cost.

overall_limitations: F31 and f32 omit the synchronous=NORMAL condition required for their consequences.
Several rubric facts are distributed across separate claims. No individual claim fully states the PASSIVE or FULL rubric entry.

The claims omit reader end-mark fixation, shared-memory lookup and host restrictions, the one-writer limit, status-counter semantics, multi-database behavior, automatic PASSIVE mode, and connection-local automatic checkpoint configuration.
No claims repeat an earlier claim with the same specifics. Related mechanisms and consequences were not treated as duplicates.
The reported pass counts and new-information rates do not establish technical depth or research saturation.
